info.codeblock:
Authentication Overview How authentication works in the API.

Authentication ensures that only authorized users and applications can access the API.

Each request must include a valid Authorization header that identifies the caller.

Supported methods include API keys and OAuth 2.0 tokens.

info.codeblock: <task id="t_authenticate_with_api_key"> <title>Authenticate with an API Key</title> <shortdesc>Use an API key to authenticate API requests.</shortdesc> <taskbody> <steps> <step> <cmd>Obtain an API key from the <uicontrol>Account Settings</uicontrol> page.</cmd> </step> <step> <cmd>Include the key in the <codeph>Authorization</codeph> header of your request.</cmd> <info> <codeph>Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY</codeph> </info> </step> <step> <cmd>Send the authenticated request and verify the response status.</cmd> </step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>

info.codeblock:
Create User Endpoint Create a new user account via the API.
Endpoint

POST /api/v1/users

Request Parameters Parameter Type Required Description email string Yes User email address
Example Request curl -X POST api.example.com/v1/users \ -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \ -d '{"email": "user@example.com"}'

step.cmd: Sample payload reference topic: Make methods with sample payloads reference topics.

info.codeblock:
Update User Method Update an existing user’s information.
Endpoint

PATCH /api/v1/users/{userId}

Example Request curl -X PATCH https://api.example.com/v1/users/123 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \ -d '{ "email": "updated@example.com", "role": "admin" }'
Example Response { "id": 123, "email": "updated@example.com", "role": "admin", "status": "active" }
